function.name: bash
function.description: Run a shell command in the local working directory. Use for git, tests, installs, and one-off scripts. Do not use it to cat/sed/head/read/write/grep source files — use the read, write, edit, and grep tools instead. If stdout is longer than 2000 lines or 50KB, the full output is saved under tools_result/bash/ and this result is head+tail only — grep or read that saved path. Do not pipe head/tail yourself. Do not use bash for the browser — use browser_exec and browser_screenshot. Do not use bash to drive desktop apps — use the computer tool. Do not launch Chrome/Chromium/Brave (no --headless, --user-data-dir, --remote-debugging-port, nohup Chrome). Do not read or copy ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a file. Text files return the lines (offset 1-based, limit). A line-number prefix appears every 10 lines, as '    10|line'. Other lines are the raw text. docx/xlsx are extracted to text: short files return inline; long ones save under tools_result/read/ and return a preview — grep or read that saved path. A .pdf is not extracted here: read the pdf skill and use bash. Do not use bash to cat or parse other files.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return

function.name: write
function.description: Create or overwrite a whole text file. Use for new files or full-file rewrites. Overwriting an existing file requires a prior read of that path; creating a new file does not. Do not use bash cat/heredoc for this. For a small in-place patch, use edit (old must be unique unless replace_all). Path is relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is). content is the full file text; empty string is allowed.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

content.description: Full file text to write. Empty string creates an empty file.

function.name: edit
function.description: Replace a snippet in an existing file. Read the file first (paginated reads count). old is exact text (not regex) copied from read without line numbers. old must appear exactly once unless replace_all is true. new may be empty to delete the snippet. Do not use this to create files — use write. Do not use bash sed for this.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

old.description: Exact text to find. Must be unique in the file unless replace_all is true. Cannot be empty.

new.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the snippet.

replace_all.description: If true, replace every occurrence of old. Default false.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents with a regex. Returns path:line:content. Optional path (file or directory, default workspace) and glob (e.g. *.py). Gitignored project files are included, such as tests/ and docs/. Skips .git, .venv, venv, node_modules, __pycache__, .agent, dist, and build. Prefer this over bash grep or bash rg. First page is 20 matches; if the footer includes cursor, call grep again with that cursor to get the next page. Do not use this to read whole files — use read.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for. Required unless cursor is set.

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the workspace.

glob.description: Only search files matching this glob, e.g. *.py or *.{ts,tsx}

cursor.description: Pagination token from a previous grep. Pass it to get the next page of the same search.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets. This is how to look something up. Answer from the snippets. If they are not enough, call web_search again with different keywords. Do not web_fetch the result links. In one user request, open at most one page, and only when one snippet is missing a fact the answer still needs. Do not use bash curl.

max_results.description: How many results to return (default 5, max 10)

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Open one public http(s) URL. Use it when the user pasted a link, or when one web_search snippet is missing a fact and that single page is required. Do not open a series of quote, index, or news pages. Do not open links from a [perplexity] search; search again instead. HTML becomes text. The full page is saved under tools_result/web_fetch/; this result is a short preview plus that path. To look inside it, grep or read that path. Do not bash the file or json.load it. Fails for private URLs, login walls, PDFs, and JavaScript-only apps.

url.description: The URL to fetch. http is upgraded to https.

function.name: memory_search
function.description: Search cross-session memory (project MEMORY.md, dated session notes, and global MEMORY.md). Use for prior decisions, how this repo is built, and user preferences. Do not use grep on the repo for that. Recalled memory is historical — verify against live files. Pass query to search; pass path (MEMORY.md, global/MEMORY.md, or a dated .md name) to read one file.

query.description: Keywords (AND). Omit when reading a file by path.

path.description: Short memory path: MEMORY.md, global/MEMORY.md, or YYYY-MM-DD-*.md

offset.description: When reading by path, 1-based start line

limit.description: When reading by path, max lines

function.name: codemode
function.description: Use it to batch independent calls, chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls. Do not use it for a single read, edit, or command. `code` is a Python async function body: await and return work. Call tools as `await tools.<name>(...)` with that tool's keyword arguments. Only print and return come back. No import, no open, no network. json, re, and math are already available. Do not import them. chr, ord, type, reversed, iter, next, divmod, pow, hex, bin, oct, ascii, and format are available. Do not call type() to inspect a value. Do not call codemode. The only tools are bash, read, write, edit, grep, web_search, web_fetch, and memory_search. There is no glob, ls, find, or list_files, and getattr is not allowed. Do not read a directory. List files with tools.bash(cmd=...) or with grep; a grep hit's path is the file. Each call is a new process, so names from an earlier codemode call are not defined. Finish in one script and print the full result, not a sample. Do not print one command just to see it. Failed calls raise. Each tools.* call returns one string, not an object. tools.read(path=, offset=, limit=) returns file text, at most 1000 lines. The footer is `[Showing lines start-end of total]`. The total line count is the number after of. If the page stops before the end, it adds `Use offset=N to continue.` A directory raises. tools.grep(pattern=, path=, glob=, cursor=) returns `path:line:content`, 20 matches per page. When more remain, the footer is `[Showing 20 of N matches. Continue with cursor="g1...."]`. Pass that cursor back as cursor=. The match count is N in `[Showing 20 of N matches]`, or N in `[Showing N matches]`. Do not report 20 or 20+. When every match fits, the footer is `[Showing N matches]`, or `[Showing 1 match]`. No matches returns a line starting with `No matches for`. tools.bash(cmd=) returns the command output text. There is no .output field. For a line count, one call with limit=1 is enough. Do not page through the file or search the file text for Use offset. Count matches from the footer or later pages in the same script, not by reading the file into the script. wc -l on more than one file adds a last line whose path is total. That line is not a file. Drop it before counting or summing.

code.description: Python async function body. await and return work. Call tools with keyword arguments.

timeout_ms.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds. Default 60000. Clamped to 1000..300000.
